problem:
If the following system of differential equations is written in the form ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ then what is the matrix $A?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)+7{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)+4{x}_{1}(t)-8{x}_{2}(t)=0\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
A first-order linear system of differential equations with two dependent variables is a system of equations that takes the following standard form:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=a(t){x}_{1}(t)+b(t){x}_{2}(t)+f(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=c(t){x}_{1}(t)+d(t){x}_{2}(t)+g(t)\end{aligned}
$$

where

- $a(t),$ $b(t),$ $c(t),$ $d(t),$ $f(t),$ and $g(t)$ are known functions, and

- ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ are unknown functions (dependent variables).

Such a system can always be written in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

where

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}a(t) & b(t) \\ c(t) & d(t)\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}f(t) \\ g(t)\end{aligned}].
$$

We have the following system.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)+7{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)+4{x}_{1}(t)-8{x}_{2}(t)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Writing our system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-7{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-4{x}_{1}(t)+8{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can rewrite our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -2 \\ -4 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

The order of a recurrence relation is the largest index difference between ${a}_{n}$ and the preceding terms in the relation.

Let's examine each recurrence relation in turn.

- The largest index difference between ${a}_{n}$ and the preceding term ${a}_{n-1}$ in the relation is $1.$ So, this recurrence relation has order $1.$

- The largest index difference between ${b}_{n}$ and the preceding terms ${b}_{n-1}$ and ${b}_{n-3}$ in the relation is $3.$ So, this recurrence relation has order $3.$

- The largest index difference between ${c}_{n}$ and the preceding term ${c}_{n-1}$ in the relation is $1.$ So, this recurrence relation has order $1.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\,{sin}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{t}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}{4}){|}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi }{4})-(-\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\pi )}{4}) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identity 

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡t=\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
